questions.title: Recover a curve from its gradient
questions.prompt_html:
A curve has gradient \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 x + 4\).

Find \(\int\left(4 x + 4\right)\,\mathrm dx\).
questions.solution_html:
Integrate \(4 x\) to \(2 x^{2}\) and \(4\) to \(4 x\).

The derivative of \(2 x^{2} + 4 x\) is \(4 x + 4\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(2 x^{2} + 4 x+C\).
questions.hint_html: Find the general antiderivative first, then substitute the point to determine the constant.

  1. Find \(\int\left(3 e^{2 x - 2}\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}}\left(3 e^{2 x - 2}\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]

  3. Find the change from \(x=\frac{3}{2}\) to \(x=2\) to 3 significant figures.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Keep \(e^{2 x - 2}\) and divide its coefficient by \(2\). Integrate any separate power term on its own.

The derivative of \(\frac{3 e^{2 x - 2}}{2}\) is \(3 e^{2 x - 2}\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(\frac{3 e^{2 x - 2}}{2}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=\frac{3 e^{2 x - 2}}{2}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[\frac{3 e^{2 x - 2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{\frac{3}{2}}=\left(\frac{3 e}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=- \frac{3}{2} + \frac{3 e}{2}\)

Answer: \(- \frac{3}{2} + \frac{3 e}{2}\).

(c)

The second interval starts at \(\frac{3}{2}\). Use these new endpoints with the same antiderivative.

\(\left[\frac{3 e^{2 x - 2}}{2}\right]_{\frac{3}{2}}^{2}=\left(\frac{3 e^{2}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{3 e}{2}\right)=\frac{3 e \left(-1 + e\right)}{2}\)

Now round the result to 3 significant figures, giving \(7.01\).

Answer: \(7.01\).

The integrand is \(6 \sec^{2}{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 1\). All angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\int\left(6 \sec^{2}{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 1\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{- \frac{\pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{24}}\left(6 \sec^{2}{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 1\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The trigonometric term integrates to tangent. The inner slope is \(2\), so include its reciprocal.

The derivative of \(- x + 3 \tan{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\) is \(6 \sec^{2}{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 1\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(- x + 3 \tan{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=- x + 3 \tan{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[- x + 3 \tan{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{24}}=\left(3 - \frac{\pi}{24}\right)-\left(\frac{\pi}{12}\right)=3 - \frac{\pi}{8}\)

Answer: \(3 - \frac{\pi}{8}\).
questions.hint_html: The two angles in the antiderivative are \(0\) and \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the antiderivative rule for each term and include the arbitrary constant.
Substitute both limits into the antiderivative and subtract in the stated order.

questions.title: Integrate a trigonometric expression in radians
questions.prompt_html:
The integrand is \(3 \sin{\left(6 x \right)} + 1\). All angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\int\left(3 \sin{\left(6 x \right)} + 1\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}}\left(3 \sin{\left(6 x \right)} + 1\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The trigonometric term integrates to negative cosine. The inner slope is \(6\), so include its reciprocal.

The derivative of \(x - \frac{\cos{\left(6 x \right)}}{2}\) is \(3 \sin{\left(6 x \right)} + 1\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(x - \frac{\cos{\left(6 x \right)}}{2}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=x - \frac{\cos{\left(6 x \right)}}{2}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[x - \frac{\cos{\left(6 x \right)}}{2}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{9}}=\left(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{\pi}{9}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{9} + \frac{3}{4}\)

Answer: \(\frac{\pi}{9} + \frac{3}{4}\).
questions.hint_html: The two angles in the antiderivative are \(0\) and \(\frac{2 \pi}{3}\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the antiderivative rule for each term and include the arbitrary constant.
Substitute both limits into the antiderivative and subtract in the stated order.

The integrand is \(3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)} + 2\). All angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\int\left(3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)} + 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{18}}\left(3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)} + 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The trigonometric term integrates to negative cosine. The inner slope is \(3\), so include its reciprocal.

The derivative of \(2 x - \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\) is \(3 \sin{\left(3 x \right)} + 2\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(2 x - \cos{\left(3 x \right)}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=2 x - \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[2 x - \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{18}}=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{9}\right)-\left(-1\right)=- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{9} + 1\)

Answer: \(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{9} + 1\).
questions.hint_html: The two angles in the antiderivative are \(0\) and \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the antiderivative rule for each term and include the arbitrary constant.
Substitute both limits into the antiderivative and subtract in the stated order.

questions.title: Integrate a trigonometric expression in radians
questions.prompt_html:
The integrand is \(3 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 2\). All angles are in radians.

  1. Find \(\int\left(3 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{- \frac{\pi}{12}}^{0}\left(3 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The trigonometric term integrates to sine. The inner slope is \(2\), so include its reciprocal.

The derivative of \(- 2 x + \frac{3 \sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{2}\) is \(3 \cos{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)} - 2\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(- 2 x + \frac{3 \sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{2}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=- 2 x + \frac{3 \sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{2}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[- 2 x + \frac{3 \sin{\left(2 x + \frac{\pi}{6} \right)}}{2}\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{12}}^{0}=\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)-\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{3}{4} - \frac{\pi}{6}\)

Answer: \(\frac{3}{4} - \frac{\pi}{6}\).
questions.hint_html: The two angles in the antiderivative are \(0\) and \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the antiderivative rule for each term and include the arbitrary constant.
Substitute both limits into the antiderivative and subtract in the stated order.

questions.title: Integrate a trigonometric expression in radians

  1. Find \(\int\left(2 - 6 \sin{\left(4 x \right)}\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{- \frac{\pi}{8}}^{0}\left(2 - 6 \sin{\left(4 x \right)}\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]

(a)

The trigonometric term integrates to sine. The inner slope is \(4\), so include its reciprocal.

The derivative of \(2 x + \frac{3 \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\) is \(2 - 6 \sin{\left(4 x \right)}\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(2 x + \frac{3 \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}+C\).

(b)

Use \(F(x)=2 x + \frac{3 \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[2 x + \frac{3 \cos{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}\right]_{- \frac{\pi}{8}}^{0}=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{3}{2}\)

Answer: \(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{3}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: The two angles in the antiderivative are \(0\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the antiderivative rule for each term and include the arbitrary constant.

questions.title: Integrate a reciprocal on a continuous branch
questions.prompt_html:
Integrate \(\frac{3}{x}\) on the branch \(x > 0\).

Find \(\int\left(\frac{3}{x}\right)\,\mathrm dx\).
questions.solution_html:
The exponent is \(-1\), so use a logarithm. Divide by the denominator's slope \(1\).

The derivative of \(3 \ln{\left(x \right)}\) is \(\frac{3}{x}\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(3\ln\left|x\right|+C\).
questions.hint_html: Evaluate the absolute value of the denominator at each endpoint, then subtract the logarithms.

questions.title: Integrate a reciprocal on a continuous branch
questions.prompt_html:
Integrate \(\frac{2}{3 x + 4}\) on the branch \(3 x + 4 > 0\).

Evaluate \(\int_{- \frac{2}{3}}^{\frac{1}{3}}\left(\frac{2}{3 x + 4}\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.
questions.solution_html:
The argument \(3 x + 4\) does not vanish between the limits. Its endpoint magnitudes are \(2\) and \(5\).

\(\frac{2}{3}\left(\ln 5-\ln 2\right)+\left(0\right)=\frac{2 \ln{\left(\frac{5}{2} \right)}}{3}\)

Answer: \(\frac{2 \ln{\left(\frac{5}{2} \right)}}{3}\).
questions.hint_html: Evaluate the absolute value of the denominator at each endpoint, then subtract the logarithms.

questions.title: Integrate a reciprocal on a continuous branch

questions.solution_html:
The argument \(2 x - 4\) does not vanish between the limits. Its endpoint magnitudes are \(1\) and \(4\).

\(1\left(\ln 4-\ln 1\right)+\left(0\right)=\ln{\left(4 \right)}\)

Answer: \(\ln{\left(4 \right)}\).

questions.title: Integrate a reciprocal on a continuous branch
questions.prompt_html:
Integrate \(-1 + \frac{6}{2 x - 1}\) on the branch \(2 x - 1 < 0\).

  1. Find \(\int\left(-1 + \frac{6}{2 x - 1}\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]

  2. Evaluate \(\int_{-4}^{- \frac{3}{2}}\left(-1 + \frac{6}{2 x - 1}\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The exponent is \(-1\), so use a logarithm. Divide by the denominator's slope \(2\).

The derivative of \(- x + 3 \ln{\left(1 - 2 x \right)}\) is \(-1 + \frac{6}{2 x - 1}\). Add the arbitrary constant.

Answer: \(3\ln\left|2 x - 1\right|- x+C\).

(b)

The argument \(2 x - 1\) does not vanish between the limits. Its endpoint magnitudes are \(9\) and \(4\).

\(3\left(\ln 4-\ln 9\right)+\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)=- \frac{5}{2} + 3 \ln{\left(\frac{4}{9} \right)}\)

Answer: \(- \frac{5}{2} + 3 \ln{\left(\frac{4}{9} \right)}\).

The derivative of \(- x + \ln{\left(- 3 x \right)}\) is \(-1 + \frac{1}{x}\). Add the arbitrary constant.

(b)

\(1\left(\ln 1-\ln 5\right)+\left(- \frac{4}{3}\right)=- \ln{\left(5 \right)} - \frac{4}{3}\)

Answer: \(- \ln{\left(5 \right)} - \frac{4}{3}\).

Let \(f(x)=4 x^{3} + 2 x + 2\).

  1. Evaluate \(\int_{-1}^{2}\left(4 x^{3} + 2 x + 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\) exactly.

    [2]

  2. Use your calculation to evaluate \(\int_{2}^{-1}\left(4 x^{3} + 2 x + 2\right)\,\mathrm dx\).

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Use \(F(x)=x^{4} + x^{2} + 2 x\). Subtract the value at the lower limit from the value at the upper limit.

\(\left[x^{4} + x^{2} + 2 x\right]_{-1}^{2}=\left(24\right)-\left(0\right)=24\)

Answer: \(24\).

(b)

Reversing the limits replaces \(F(b)-F(a)\) by \(F(a)-F(b)\).

\(\left[x^{4} + x^{2} + 2 x\right]_{2}^{-1}=\left(0\right)-\left(24\right)=-24\)

Answer: \(-24\).
